function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Here’s a quick snapshot of the most widely celebrated “festivals” (public holidays, parades, and seasonal celebrations) that will take place in the United States after **October 19, 2026**.  (If you’re looking for a particular type of festival—music, food, cultural, etc.—you can let me know and I’ll dig deeper.)

| # | Festival / Event | Dates (2026) | Typical Locations | What Happens |
|---|------------------|--------------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Oktoberfest – New York City** | Oct 20–23 | Brooklyn, NY (Brooklyn Bridge Park) | German‑style beer tents, bratwurst, pretzels, live music, carnival rides. |
| 2 | **Halloween** | Nov 1 | Nationwide (especially NYC, LA, Chicago, Miami) | Trick‑or‑treating, costume parties, haunted houses, pumpkin carving contests. |
| 3 | **Veterans Day Parade** | Nov 11 | Washington, D.C. (and many cities nationwide) | Military floats, marching bands, patriotic speeches, community booths. |
| 4 | **Thanksgiving Day Parade** | Nov 24 | New York City (Broadway & Central Park) | Giant balloons, marching bands, celebrity performers, holiday cheer. |
| 5 | **Black Friday** | Nov 25 | Nationwide (major malls, department stores, online) | Door‑buster sales, early‑morning crowds, flash deals. |
| 6 | **Cyber Monday** | Nov 28 | Nationwide (online retailers) | Online discounts, limited‑time offers, free shipping promotions. |
| 7 | **Christmas** | Dec 25 | Nationwide (homes, churches, malls) | Tree lighting, Santa visits, gift exchanges, caroling, nativity scenes. |
| 8 | **New Year’s Eve (Times Square)** | Dec 31 | New York City (Times Square) | Countdown, fireworks, live music, midnight kiss, massive crowds. |

### Quick Highlights

* **Oktoberfest NYC** – The largest German‑culture celebration outside Germany, featuring authentic Bavarian cuisine, craft beers, and a lively atmosphere.  
* **Thanksgiving Parade** – One of the world’s most iconic holiday parades, drawing millions of viewers worldwide.  
* **New Year’s Eve Times Square** – The quintessential global celebration, complete with the famous ball drop and a vibrant crowd of thousands.

---

#### How to Make the Most of These Events

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Book accommodations early** | Popular events attract visitors from all over the country. |
| **Arrive early for parades** | Secure good viewing spots and avoid long lines. |
| **Check local COVID‑19 guidelines** | Some events may still have health protocols in place. |
| **Plan transportation** | Public transit can be crowded; consider rideshares or parking passes. |
| **Stay hydrated & wear comfortable shoes** | Long days outdoors can be tiring. |

Let me know if you’d like more details on a specific festival, such as ticket prices, travel itineraries, or lesser‑known regional celebrations!
